context: The plan is not a first-class object: it is the implicit set of TASK records plus the gate conditions G2/G3 (CORE/gates/gates.json), and the PLAN READY gate closes on expertise-level manual_attestation (G3.5) that references 'the plan' without a shared identifier. DESIGN-01 (ARCH-CONVERGENCE-001) closes the execution-integrity chain TASK->PLAN->CONSENT->EXECUTION->ARTIFACTS->DIGESTS->RESULT->EVIDENCE->VERIFICATION->CHECKPOINT: consent (G3.5) and execution receipts (EEX-1, documented in DOCS/EXECUTION_INTEGRITY.md) need a stable identity for the approved plan. SHA-256 content digesting already exists as a capability of the generation pipeline (SCRIPTS/se_core/opencode/generator.py), used for drift detection of the generated adapter tree.
problem: How to give the approved plan a deterministic, stable identity that consent and execution receipts can reference, without introducing a PLAN record type, a PLAN schema, or any runtime mechanism?

options_considered.option: Introduce a PLAN record type and schema
cons: New record lifecycle (CORE artifact-types, SCHEMAS, RECORD_TYPES, templates, coverage, commands)
Duplicates the task-set it would project
No single plan file exists today (plan = the task collection)
File snapshots drift and need maintenance

options_considered.option: Deterministic digest function over the canonical task-set (pure function)
cons: Requires a precise canonical serialization spec
Recomputable only with a matching generator function

decision: Adopt EPI-1 as a convention/pure function. PLAN_ID = sha256(canonical_json({project_id, tasks: [semantic_projection per TASK]})). The canonical task-set is the project's TASK records with status != CANCELLED; tasks are ordered by id; serialization is compact JSON with sorted keys and sorted set-arrays; the semantic projection includes id, type, title, objective, scope, parent_task, subtasks, dependencies, related_requirements, authorized_actions, acceptance_criteria, verification, capability_policy; excluded fields are status, evidence, metadata, timestamps, owner. An empty plan is not approvable (G3.1 tasks_present) and no receipt may reference it; if any task in the set fails schema validation, PLAN_ID is UNDEFINED (not computed). SHA-256 is the same content-digest capability previously introduced in generator.py; generator.py is not modified. No PLAN record, no PLAN schema, no runtime implementation, no migration.
reason: The plan is already the task-set plus gates; an identity derived deterministically from that set closes the traceability link at near-zero cost and extends existing mechanics (SHA-256, ADR-0014 guidance semantics) instead of creating parallel architecture.
consequences: Plan identity is a documented convention (DOCS/EXECUTION_INTEGRITY.md) referenced by consent attestations (G3.5) and execution receipts (EEX-1). Structural changes to the plan (add/remove a task, or change any included field) produce a different PLAN_ID and invalidate prior attestations. Irrelevant metadata changes (status, evidence, owner, timestamps, free metadata) preserve the identity. A future optional `se plan-digest` command would require this specification plus a separate change event (ADR + tests + doctor) and is explicitly not part of this decision.
